mentioned.quote: Offensive Cybersecurity: When an AI’s capabilities could facilitate cybersecurity threats, necessitating strict, proactive measures.

threshold.quote: Automating powerful cyber offensive operations against unsecured or secured targets, in a way that could cause critical damage.
threshold.note: Frontier Capability Threshold table, Offensive cybersecurity row.

response.quote: Each capability threshold is associated with a required Deployment Mitigation Level (DML) and Security Mitigation Levels (SML), which must be achieved before the capability threshold is reached.
response.note: Threshold table (p.5-6) maps this risk to DML 2 and SML 2; measures listed p.7-10 (real-time classifiers, controlled rollout to trusted users; role-based weight access, geofencing, network segmentation).

acc_decider.quote: A dedicated Frontier AI Governance Board, composed of our Chief Responsible AI Officer, Head of Responsible AI, Head of Technology Risk, and General Counsel, shall oversee all frontier model operations, reviewing safety protocols, risk assessments, and escalation decisions.
acc_decider.note: Named board with listed members; also 'Evaluating Model Compliance' and investigating non-compliance (p.11). Capability results go to this Board and the G42 Executive Leadership Committee (p.5).

acc_external.quote: External Audits: To reinforce accountability, G42 will engage in annual external audits to verify compliance with the Framework.
acc_external.note: Framework-wide adherence audit; also p.12 'An annual external review of the Framework will be conducted to ensure adequacy'.

acc_unmet.quote: If a necessary Deployment Mitigation Level cannot be achieved, then the model’s deployment must be restricted; if a necessary Security Mitigation Level cannot be achieved, then further capabilities development of the model must be paused.
